segments.contextAfter: The ray needs to fully intersect a primitive for a hit to be detected. In particular, it is not enough for the ray to precisely tangent or end at the primitive’s surface. This becomes especially important when ray casting against primitives that are far away from the ray origin.

segments.source: The ray needs to fully intersect a primitive for a hit to be detected. In particular, it is not enough for the ray to precisely tangent or end at the primitive’s surface. This becomes especially important when ray casting against primitives that are far away from the ray origin.
segments.normalizedSource: The ray needs to fully intersect a primitive for a hit to be detected. In particular, it is not enough for the ray to precisely tangent or end at the primitive’s surface. This becomes especially important when ray casting against primitives that are far away from the ray origin.
segments.contextBefore: The following are some details to keep in mind.
segments.contextAfter: Due to numerical imprecision, it may be necessary to use a slightly longer ray length than your desired maximum distance in order to ensure that a full intersection occurs with your target primitive. Moreover, the length of the ray needs to be a positive finite number that is smaller than `greatestFiniteMagnitude`.
